idiom_name: Sequelize belongsToMany over an explicit through model
implementation_notes: In Node the association is mapped by the ORM: Sequelize's belongsToMany declares the many-to-many and the through model is the join table, declared as a string for the shorthand form or as a real model when the link needs columns, constraints or scopes. Instances then mutate the association with generated accessors (add, remove, set, count), which issue the INSERT and DELETE against the join table, and reads go through get with an include. On a document store there is no join table at all: Mongoose keeps an array of ObjectId references and populate() resolves them, which is the right shape only because MongoDB has no relational schema to normalise.
pitfalls: A string through is a shorthand with no model: payload columns, scopes and per-link queries all require defining the through model instead.

Uniqueness of the pair is a schema concern, not an ORM guarantee: declare a unique index (or a composite primary key) on the two foreign keys of the through table, or repeated add calls accumulate duplicate links.
Nested includes over many-to-many associations multiply rows and can be extremely slow; restrict the join-table attributes or query the through model directly.

On MongoDB there is no join table at all - Mongoose stores an array of ObjectId references and populate() resolves them per document, so an association that must be queried from both sides relationally belongs in a relational store.
